paras: Cyrtodactylus jaegeri is a species of gecko, a lizard in the family Gekkonidae. The species is endemic to Laos.
The specific name, jaegeri, is in honor of German arachnologist Peter Jäger.
C. jaegeri is found in Khammouane Province, Laos.
The preferred natural habitats of C. jaegeri are forest and rocky areas, at an altitude of 170 m (560 ft).

C. jaegeri differs from other species of Indo-Chinese Cyrtodactylus by having a maximum snout-vent length (SVL) of 68.5 millimetres (2.70 in); its dorsal pattern consisting of a dark loop and four brown bands between limb insertions; dorsal tubercles in 15–17 irregular rows; lateral skin folds with dispersed tubercles; enlarged femoral scales present; and its subcaudal tubercles transversely enlarged.
The mode of reproduction of C. jaegeri is unknown.
